sections.h2: Where do I take a deed in Warren County, and when is the counter staffed?
sections.html:
Find the Warren County deeds office at 109 South Main Street in Warrenton. Staff are at the counter on weekdays, half past eight until five. The mailing address is P.O. Box 506, Warrenton, NC 27589, and the phone number printed on the office website is (252) 257-3265.

Voters choose the register every two years, as G.S. 161-1. To learn who owns a parcel here, bring an owner name: the staff look records up by name only. Callers with only an address are sent to the tax office.

The county manager's page says Warren County dates to 1779, was named for a physician killed at Bunker Hill, spans 443 square miles of rolling fields and has some 20,000 residents. A five-member board of commissioners governs it under a council-manager system. With so small a population, one counter serves the whole county, and a phone call often settles a question before you drive in.

sections.h2: What does recording a deed in Warren County actually do?
sections.html:
Recording a deed is what protects a buyer in a priority dispute. Under G.S. 47-18, a transfer, or a lease running past three years, gains no force against lien creditors or paying purchasers until registered. The earlier registration time wins.

The office's own description is short: it lets an owner announce an interest in real estate to everyone. Its files are open to any member of the public. Beyond land, it holds birth records for births in Warren County, marriage licenses and notary oaths, and it records DD-214 discharge papers for retired military without a charge.

  • Land records take deeds, mortgages, releases, plats and powers of attorney.
  • Wills are not kept here; probate belongs to the courthouse clerk.
  • For liens and judgments the office's FAQ points to the clerk of court at (252) 257-6300.

sections.h2: What will Warren County charge to record my deed?
sections.html:
The statewide schedule in G.S. 161-10 governs here. It prices an ordinary deed at $26 through page 15, then $4 for each page past that. Mortgages and deeds of trust run $64 through page 35, again with $4 for each extra page. Releasing a mortgage is free.

The table lists the figures a home seller meets most often.

Warren County's own fee page and FAQ carry older wording, including a different charge per extra page and an old deeds of trust figure. Phone the register for a total before you send anything, and treat the statute as the baseline.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax on a Warren County deed?
sections.html:
The seller bears this tax. The rate is a dollar for every $500, or part of $500, of the price or value, and it must be paid to the county's register before the deed goes on record.

Revenue is split: one half supports the county's general fund and the other half goes to the state each month, less a small allowance. The statute spells this out.

An older office FAQ writes the same rate as $2 per $1,000. Since the stamp tracks the price, read the exact figure off the settlement statement from the closing attorney.

sections.h2: What should a Warren County seller check before the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Verify three points: names on the deed match the title, the tax account is current, and the paper meets the office's format rules. A recording checklist and fee page sit on the register's website, and staff take questions by phone.

  • Adding or removing a name means a new deed. The office says to use an attorney, then record it at the usual fee, with excise tax if a price applies.
  • Look up the account at the county tax office. Bills fall due each September 1, and interest begins after January 5 under G.S. 105-360.
  • Ask the clerk whether any lien or judgment is on file.
  • Bring cash, a check or a money order: the FAQ says the office takes no credit cards.

A call to the register and the tax office before you list costs nothing and removes surprises.

sections.h2: How does Warren County's rural setting affect a sale?
sections.html:
Rural parcels, farm tracts and family land are common in a county this size. Such sales can bring a survey, a plat or an easement, each recorded on its own line.

State law prices a plat at $21 a sheet. If you are splitting acreage, ask the register what format the plat needs before the surveyor finishes. For tax maps, parcel numbers and aerial maps, the register's FAQ sends callers to the county tax mapping office at (252) 257-4158.

Heirs planning to sell should check whether any deed was ever recorded in their names. Estate paperwork may need the clerk first, then the register.

The office FAQ lists copies of recorded maps at five cents a page, larger maps at fifty cents, and deed copies at five cents a page. Scanned deeds can be viewed through the online search.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Warren County house that has liens or repairs due?
sections.html:
Yes. A closing attorney pays off liens and unpaid taxes out of the price and records the releases. A worn-out house can still sell to a buyer who takes it in its current state.

Order a title search early so the register's index and the clerk's judgments are both checked. To see a cash price for a Warren County house beside a listing price, ask this site for an offer.

faqs.q: Is releasing a Warren County mortgage free?
faqs.a: Yes. State law sets no fee for recording a satisfaction of a deed of trust or mortgage, and the Warren office lists cancellations the same way.

faqs.q: Can Warren County staff name a parcel's owner from an address?
faqs.a: No. Staff search by owner name only and send callers without a name to the tax office.

faqs.q: Does the Warren County deeds office file wills?
faqs.a: No. Wills and estates go through the clerk of superior court. The register handles deeds, mortgages, plats, releases, marriage licenses and notary oaths.

faqs.q: Does Warren County charge to record a DD-214?
faqs.a: No. The office says it records discharge papers for retired military free.

faqs.q: Who answers deed questions in Warren County?
faqs.a: Call the register at (252) 257-3265 on a weekday between half past eight and five. The office is at 109 South Main Street in Warrenton.
